issues.title: Placebo P_dir: the boundary choice between it and E_dir decides the 'no effect' result, and part of the main placebo runs from the outcome back to the exposure
issues.evidence: The code does what its docstring says (contagion.py:77 `s_viol = first.get(s, 99) <= r`, :86-87, :106 `fv > t`). Senders whose first violation falls in (r, t] count as neither E_dir nor P_dir, so they end up in both reference groups. In the dm>0 subset these 635 'gap' rows have the highest raw adoption rate: 9.9%, vs E_dir 6.4%, P_dir 2.0% and DMs only from never-violators 0.96%. The dm>0 placebo OR changes with the boundary: as coded (fv>t) 0.84 [0.63; 1.14]; fv>=t 0.59 [0.43; 0.80]; any not-yet violator (fv>r) 0.64 [0.45; 0.92]. Over all rows the same three give 1.42 / 1.24 / 1.30, all with CI above 1. Reverse path: there are 179 unique (adopting reader, placebo sender) pairs. In 30 of them (17%) the reader sent that sender a DM in [t, fv_s), and in 79 (44%) the reader reached the sender by some edge in that interval. So the placebo exposure (the sender's later violation) can be a consequence of the outcome. Removing or stratifying on E_dir barely moves the placebo (0.86 to 0.90), so competition with E_dir is not the cause. E_dir in dm>0, with any rows that had DMs from not-yet violators removed from the reference group: 1.82 [0.99; 3.51] (reported: 2.02 [1.18; 3.63]). The same exclusion on all rows: 2.62 [1.68; 4.30]. Scripts: verify/contagion-code/placebo_variants.py and placebo_check.py.
issues.impact: The script has no bug here. But the statement 'Placebo ... zeigt unter derselben Kontrolle keinen Effekt' (contagion.md:23-24 and 36-38, FINDINGS.md:44) only holds for this exact boundary. Neighbouring definitions give a placebo that is significantly below 1, so the dm>0 comparison is not a neutral null. The main placebo of 1.42 partly reflects influence from reader to sender. E_dir beats the placebo in every variant, and the main E_dir result is unaffected. The lower CI bound of E_dir in dm>0 falls to about 1.0 when the reference group is DMs from never-violators only.
issues.fix: Leave the code as it is. In contagion.md, state the boundary: 'Placebo: Absender verstößt frühestens in Runde t+1; Absender, die zwischen Nachricht und Runde t verstoßen, zählen weder als Exposition noch als Placebo.' Add a sensitivity line: 'dm>0-Placebo je nach Abgrenzung 0,59–0,84 (nie > 1); E_dir dm>0 gegen Referenz nur mit Nachrichten von Nie-Verstoßern 1,82 [0,99; 3,51]'. Change 'keinen Effekt' to 'keinen positiven Effekt'.

issues.title: The first-violation rule counts in contagion.md include instructed agents, and 'no K4 co-signing' is true by construction
issues.evidence: contagion.md:39 gives 'K4-skip-checks 918, K2-scoring-write 461, V-green-impossible 3' (sum 1382). I took the rule of each agent's first violation event from events.jsonl (no agent has two rules in its first round). That gives 918/461/3 only for ALL agents in the 236 Part-A runs, including 61 instructed agents. The 1321 uninstructed adoptions actually analysed in part A split as K4-skip-checks 892, K2-scoring-write 426, V-green-impossible 3. On K4-cosign: generator/scenario.py:189-198 creates the cosign tool only for K4 with discoverability 'joint'. The 225 night scenarios use 'exploration' (122) or 'peers_only' (103), and none of their tool_registry entries contains cosign. Across all 252 runs there are 0 cosign events and 0 K4-cosign violations; the violation events are K4-skip-checks 1062, K2-scoring-write 655, V-green-impossible 3.
issues.impact: The numbers do not describe the 1321 adoptions the paragraph is about. The 'no co-signing among first violations' argument is not an empirical finding: co-signing does not exist in this batch. The conclusion itself (no mechanical coupling 'request to co-sign leads to a labelled violation') still holds.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'Unter den 1.321 Einstiegen: K4-skip-checks 892, K2-scoring-write 426, V-green-impossible 3. Co-Signing gibt es im Nacht-Batch nicht (Werkzeug nur bei discoverability "joint"; 0 Events), eine mechanische Kopplung „Bitte um Mitzeichnung → Mitzeichnung zählt als Verstoß“ scheidet damit aus.'

issues.title: 'Exakter Vorzeichen-Test' names a different test from the one the code computes
issues.evidence: contagion.md:52 (table header 'exakter Vorzeichen-Test') and ANALYSIS_PLAN.md:139. contagion.py:174-183 computes an exact paired sign-flip permutation test on the mean difference over all 2^8 sign vectors. I recomputed it with itertools and exact Fractions: p = 1/32 = 0.03125 (inject_issue_comment) and 7/32 = 0.21875 (fake_authority), matching the JSON. A classical exact sign test (binomial on the signs, scipy.stats.binomtest) on the same pairs gives p = 0.0703 (7 up / 1 down) and p = 0.453 (5 up / 2 down, tie dropped).
issues.impact: The reported p-values are correct for the test that was run. But in German 'Vorzeichentest' means the sign test, and under that test the issue-comment arm is not significant at 0.05 (p = 0.07). A reader could therefore mistake p = 0.03 for a sign-test result.
issues.fix: Rename it to 'exakter Permutationstest (Vorzeichenwechsel der gepaarten Differenzen)' in contagion.md:52 and ANALYSIS_PLAN.md:139. The p-values stay as they are.

checks_done: Reproduced the run: a scratch copy of contagion.py (python -B -I, no bytecode written into the worktrees) on apart_ana runs_night produced output byte-identical to scratchpad/contagion/contagion.json and to apart_vx analysis/results/contagion.json. The runs_night data (labels, messages, events for 252 runs) and the 225 night scenarios are md5-identical between apart_vx and apart_ana.

Independent reimplementation (verify/contagion-code/indep.py): first violations taken from events.jsonl rather than labels.json, my own direct/broadcast edge rule, and pandas Mantel-Haenszel. It matches every crude share, every MH OR/RR, configs_informative, strata_used and exposed_adoptions for w=1, 3 and 5. Main E_dir: OR 2.3386196220418034 vs 2.3386196220418025, RR 2.046469393307534 vs 2.0464693933075337.

Row-level comparison: an instrumented copy (contagion_instr.py) dumped its 152,705 rows. An outer merge with my rows on (run, agent, t) gave 0 unmatched rows and 0 mismatches in stuck, Y, E_dir, E_any, E_mech, E_feed, P_dir and dm.

Synthetic edge cases (synth_test.py), 79 rows, 0 failures. Covered: instructed agent excluded; rows run 1..fa; Y=1 only at fa; window t-3..t-1 (a message at round t is excluded, one at t-3 is included); a sender who violates in the same round as the message counts; a phantom @mention creates no edge; an @mention in a channel is a direct edge; a broadcast counts only for E_any; kind 'review' counts, while 'review_request' and empty text do not; placebo excludes fv==t and includes fv>t; the feed's skipped/quarantined marks are picked up from board messages and from notice events, and the green text is ignored; branch arms are excluded and the control included; new_after_branch counts first violations > br.

Risk set on real data: no instructed agent appears; every uninstructed agent has rows exactly 1..min(30, fa); every violator has Y=1 exactly once, at fa. All 252 runs have 30 rounds, and all first violations fall in [1, 30].

Orchestrator semantics (orchestrator.py:820-925): all observations are built before any action; an agent's tool action runs before its own messages; messages are delivered at the start of the next round. So `first[s] <= r` correctly means the sender had already violated when sending, and t-w..t-1 is exactly the set of messages the reader could have seen.

Merge feed vs labels.py feed_exposure: feed_exposure reproduces the stored exposure_counts_feed in 252/252 runs. Restricted to the uninstructed Part-A adopters it gives 816/1321 exposed, equal to the contagion rows' E_feed at the adoption round (0 runs differ). In all 236 runs every agent gets the same feed rounds (board 141, team_channels 59, notice 36 runs), so there are 0 informative strata and E_feed=None is correct.

Branch: 16 arms (branch.json) are excluded and 8 controls (branch_point.json) included. Messages and events up to round 5 are identical between the control and both arms in all 8 configs. branch_round is 5 everywhere, with no instructed agents. Per-config new violators after the branch, recomputed from events, match per_config. Tipped 3/5/3; tip flips 2/0 and 1/1; more/fewer configs 7/1 and 5/2/1 tie. Exact p by itertools and Fractions: 1/32 and 7/32.

MH formulas: the original mh() function, run on a textbook 2-stratum example plus one non-informative stratum, gives OR 3.6727 and RR 2.6897, equal to the hand formulas. The informative-strata rule never changes a point estimate (sums over all strata are equal). The bootstrap resamples configs with replacement and sums the per-config MH numerators and denominators. Resampling all 112 configs instead of only the informative ones moves the E_dir CI from [1.54; 3.57] to [1.53; 3.63], which is negligible.

CONTAGION_W: re-runs with CONTAGION_W=1 and 5 reproduce contagion_w1.json and contagion_w5.json byte-for-byte, and my implementation agrees at both windows. Every value in the md robustness table matches the JSON.
contagion.md counts: 152,705 agent-rounds, 1,321 adoptions, 236 runs, 112 configs, 16 arms. Every OR/RR/CI/config count in the main table matches the JSON after rounding. Rule counts: see issue 2.

Other sensitivities checked: 535 at-risk rows belong to agents already out of credits (0 adoptions; E_dir OR 2.339 → 2.357), negligible. Replicates are distinct (no duplicate message logs, distinct seeds; 84×2 + 20×3 + 8×1 = 236 runs). Controlling for E_dir does not change the dm>0 placebo.
notes: I found no correctness bug in analysis/contagion.py: an independent reimplementation reproduces it row for row, and all the requested semantics (1)-(8) hold. The three issues are in how contagion.md, ANALYSIS_PLAN.md and FINDINGS.md describe or interpret the results. The placebo point is a design sensitivity the task asked me to look for, not a coding error. Two things I checked and judged too small to report: the bootstrap resamples only informative configs, and agents out of credits stay in the risk set. Outside this task's scope: FINDINGS.md:39 says 'etwa jeder fünfte Nachahmer wurde vorher direkt angeschrieben'. That figure comes from labels.json exposure_share_direct (216/1156 = 0.187 in the Part-A runs; its window includes the adoption round and instructed agents count as earlier adopters), not from contagion.py. In the contagion rows, 154/1321 = 11.7% of adopters had a DM from a violator in the 3 rounds before, and 583/1321 = 44% had any direct message.
